# AuthZEN.guide

> A practical guide to OpenID AuthZEN, the OpenID Foundation standard for externalized, fine-grained authorization. The Authorization API 1.0 (Final Specification, approved 12 January 2026) defines a JSON-over-HTTPS API that a Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) uses to ask a Policy Decision Point (PDP) whether a subject can perform an action on a resource in a given context. Maintained by David Brossard (CTO, Axiomatics; co-chair of the OpenID AuthZEN WG; editor of the Authorization API 1.0).

Key facts:
- Request: subject {type, id, properties?}, action {name, properties?}, resource {type, id, properties?}, context? → response: {decision: boolean, context?}
- Default endpoints: /access/v1/evaluation, /access/v1/evaluations (batch), /access/v1/search/subject, /access/v1/search/resource, /access/v1/search/action
- Discovery: /.well-known/authzen-configuration
- Policy-language neutral: ALFA/XACML, Rego, Cedar or ReBAC engines can all serve AuthZEN.

## Guide

- [What is OpenID AuthZEN](https://authzen.guide/): overview, status, how it works, FAQ
- [API reference with JSON examples](https://authzen.guide/api): evaluation, batch, search, PDP metadata
- [Implementations](https://authzen.guide/implementations): PDPs, API gateways and IdPs that support AuthZEN
- [AuthZEN vs XACML, OPA, Cedar, OpenFGA](https://authzen.guide/compare): how AuthZEN relates to policy languages and engines

## Normative sources

- [Authorization API 1.0 (Final)](https://openid.net/specs/authorization-api-1_0.html)
- [OpenID AuthZEN Working Group](https://openid.net/wg/authzen/)
